Summary: The holiness call: be holy, for the LORD your God is holy — the summons that opens the holiness code. Doubt: Umbrella call rather than a distinct command: it introduces the whole holiness code and could fold into the moral laws as a group instead of standing alone.
Commandment: Be holy, for the LORD your God is holy.
Application: Peter carries the same call into the church: as obedient children, be holy in all your conduct. Holiness here is both a gift and a command.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: because the LORD your God is holy (Leviticus 19:2); Peter reissues the same call to the church (1 Peter 1:15-16).
Function: This law names a duty that does not expire: it is about character, not procedure. The holiness call: be holy, for the LORD your God is holy — the summons that opens the holiness code. Scripture gives the reason: because the LORD your God is holy; Peter reissues the same call to the church. No particular evil is named here; its work was likeness to a holy God, not restraint.
